text.tspan: Automatic segmentation of Bumps in neural data PSD
A. Generation of synthetic data for supervised learning
Clean PSD is generated using a randomized combination of
and power law decay multiplied by a scaling factor. This produces
localized bumps at specific frequencies and power law decay.
Locally it mimic the shapes observed in neural data, where it
is custom to decompose signal into aperiodic (power law decay)
and oscillatory components (bumps). The goal here is to generate
a dataset that does not reflect exact psds of neural data, but that contains
all the shape elements. This way a neural network that learned to work on
these shapes on a large variety of curves can be applied to real neural data.
To mimic the noise one would obtain using a Welch method to get the PSD we
use a chi-squared distribution to model it.
The input of the neural network is the noisy PSD. It has three different outputs.
The cleaned PSD, a heatmap of the peak location and the left/right width offset.
The cleaned PSD corresponds to a smoothing of the noisy input. The heatmap
is a value between 0 and 1. The closer to 1 the higher to probability to be a peak, and
for 0 to be background. Finally the left/rigth widths offset represents at a given frequency
inside the interval of a bump by how much one should move to the left/right to find the
The clean PSD, target heatmap and left/rigth widths offset are given as supervised data for the
network to learn mapping between noisy psd input and the three ouptuts.
The architecture backbone is a low depth 2 layers U-Net for 1D processing of data.
Standard convolution are replaced by residual convolution blocks in the encoder and
in tge decoder after its up convolution layer. After the U-net the feature maps are passed through
three heads. They all consists of a sequence of convolution layer + GELU + convolution layer.
The one for the heatmap is followed by a sigmoid activation to transfrom output logits into
probabilty score in [0, 1]. The one for the left/right edges is followed by Softplus to ensure
The losses used depends on the heads. For the clean PSD head, we use
the PSD MAE to get reconstruction of the curve. The first order derivative
MAE to focus on slopes and maxima of peaks. The second order derivative
MAE to focus on smooth curve and avoid fluctuations.
For the heatmap we used the center Focal Loss. Finally, for the offsets we use
for the left and right the MAE of the curve and add a background loss (to explain)
Around each peak, we segment the left and right boundary of the bump.
